evals.prompt: In F# with FSharpPlus 1.9.1, define a binary tree type `Tree<'T> = Leaf of 'T | Node of Tree<'T> * Tree<'T>` and make it work with F#+'s generic `map` and `traverse`, so that `map ((+) 1) tree : Tree<int>` and `traverse (fun x -> if x > 0 then Some x else None) tree : Tree<int> option` both compile and behave correctly. The script must start with `#r "nuget: FSharpPlus, 1.9.1"`, define the type with whatever static members are needed, and end with `printfn "%A"` lines showing map and traverse applied to `Node (Leaf 1, Node (Leaf 2, Leaf 3))` and traverse applied to `Node (Leaf 1, Leaf -2)`.

The F# script `validation-short-circuit.fsx` in the current directory (FSharpPlus 1.9.1) does not do what the author wants. They want both validation errors accumulated, so the program prints a failure containing both "empty name" and "bad age", and they want the final value converted to a plain `Result<string * int, string list>` before printing. Fix it. The corrected script must start with `#r "nuget: FSharpPlus, 1.9.1"` and end with a `printfn "%A"` of the Result value.

Using FSharpPlus 1.9.1, write an F# script that uses the `ReaderT` monad transformer over `Result<_, string>`. Define `type Config = { BaseUrl: string }`. Define `buildUrl (path: string)` in that stack: it reads the config and returns `Error "empty path"` when the path is empty, otherwise `Ok (config.BaseUrl + "/" + path)`. Define `both` using the `monad` computation expression that calls `buildUrl "users"` and `buildUrl "orders"` and returns the tuple. Run `both` and also `buildUrl ""` against `{ BaseUrl = "https://example.com" }` and print both results with `printfn "%A"`. The script must start with `#r "nuget: FSharpPlus, 1.9.1"`.

This F# snippet using FSharpPlus 1.9.1 fails with FS0030 (value restriction):

```fsharp
#r "nuget: FSharpPlus, 1.9.1"
open FSharpPlus
let increment = map ((+) 1)
let a = increment [1; 2]
let b = increment (Some 5)
printfn "%A %A" a b
```

Fix it so that `increment` still works on both a list and an option, and the script prints `[2; 3] Some 6`. The script must start with `#r "nuget: FSharpPlus, 1.9.1"`.

Using FSharpPlus 1.9.1, define a single-case wrapper `type Box<'T> = Box of 'T` and give it the static members F#+ needs so that all of the following compile and run: `map ((+) 1) (Box 1)`, `result 2 : Box<int>`, `Box ((+) 1) <*> Box 2`, `bind (fun x -> Box (x * 2)) (Box 3)`, and a `monad { let! x = Box 1 in let! y = Box 2 in return x + y }` block typed as `Box<int>`. Print each value with `printfn "%A"` in that order. The script must start with `#r "nuget: FSharpPlus, 1.9.1"`.
